newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil voters do not understand re-election - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil voters do not understand re-election - paper.

text.p: About one third of Brazilian voters do not fully understand the definition of "re-election," a newspaper survey said on Friday.
A survey by the Ibope research institute showed 19 percent of the 2,000 voters interviewed did not know what the term meant or said they ignored the meaning of it, O Globo said.
Fourteen percent of the voters believed re-election meant office holders would have their terms renewed automatically at the end of their mandate, according to the survey.
The survey also found that 51 percent approved of giving President Fernando Henrique Cardoso a chance to run for a second term, O Globo said.

Of the 49 percent who disapproved, 25 percent were against re-election in principal, 19 percent believed the right to run for re-election should only come into force with the next president and five percent gave no opinion.
The debate on a constitutional amendment that would allow Cardoso to run for a second presidential term was expected to dominate Brazilian politics in the coming months.
